name: Research, Knowledge and Learning
blurb: How the field explains itself: papers and their venues, books, courses and certifications, the skills graph, the glossary and taxonomy, and the media record of talks and podcasts.

domains.name: AI Research Library
domains.blurb: The AI Research Library has two layers. The first is a curated shelf of 320 peer-reviewed and preprint papers, organised into 12 topics from architectures and reasoning to bias, evaluation, security and the EU AI Act, each with its authors, venue, year and citation count, a short note on why it matters, and, where the abstract is on file, three explanations written for a beginner, a practitioner and a business reader.

domains.name: AI in Education
domains.blurb: What works for AI in schools from preschool to graduation, built on the book The AI Ready School: the classroom by subject and grade, every student and family, and running the school, with the evidence for each idea.

domains.name: Education and the Skills Graph
domains.blurb: Books, courses, and certifications, mapped to a skills graph with prerequisites, employers, and salary ranges.

sections.name: AI Books
sections.blurb: Books by topic, difficulty, and audience, with companion code.

sections.name: AI Courses
sections.blurb: University and platform courses, with duration, cost, and what they actually teach.

sections.name: AI Certifications
sections.blurb: Vendor and vendor-neutral certifications, cost, renewal, and employer recognition.

sections.name: AI Skills Graph
sections.blurb: Every skill mapped to its prerequisites, related skills, learning paths, employers, and salary range.

domains.name: Glossary and Taxonomy
domains.blurb: Every term, acronym, protocol, architecture, and algorithm, explained once per audience and linked into a navigable concept graph.

sections.name: AI Glossary
sections.blurb: 522 AI terms defined in plain English, each with origin, example, and related terms.

sections.name: Understand AI
sections.blurb: The glossary in the order the ideas build, for a reader who does not yet know what to ask.

domains.name: Universal Knowledge Graph
domains.blurb: The connective tissue: every entity linked to every other relevant entity, so the site is navigable rather than a pile of pages.

sections.name: Entity Graph
sections.blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

sections.name: Relationships
sections.blurb: Who built what, what trained on what, what cites what, and what regulates what.

domains.name: Concept Taxonomy
domains.blurb: The chain from transformer to attention to KV cache to inference to GPU to cloud, navigable in both directions.

domains.name: AI Media and Visual Repository
domains.blurb: Keynotes, conference talks, tutorials, podcasts with transcripts, and a diagram and image library.

sections.name: Video Library
sections.blurb: This section covers video worth watching on AI: vendor keynotes where model and hardware announcements land, practitioner conference talks, university course lecture series, and standalone explainers that became the field's default onboarding.

sections.name: Podcasts
sections.blurb: This section curates podcasts covering AI research, engineering, and industry strategy, tracking each show's host, focus, and whether transcripts are published, rather than pulling from a live episode feed or download-ranking data.

sections.name: Image and Diagram Library
sections.blurb: This section curates freely usable images, diagrams, and interactive visualizations for explaining AI concepts, covering architecture diagrams, illustrated walkthroughs, and browser-based model explorers, rather than hosting original...

reading.body:
Of the 771 pages under this section, 553 are glossary entries alone, meaning the glossary and taxonomy is by far the largest single component of how this site explains AI to itself, more than five times the size of the 147-page research library.

The six domains here split into three functions, explaining terms through the 553-page glossary, curating external learning material through 49 pages of courses, certifications, and books, and connecting everything together through the research library's 147 papers, the knowledge graph's 3 pages, and the 1-page concept taxonomy. The video, podcast, and image library adds 18 more pages of media rather than text, a comparatively small share of the section's total.

The size imbalance between the glossary and everything else is itself informative. A reference site that defines 553 distinct terms but curates only 19 courses and 9 certifications is investing far more in breadth of vocabulary than in structured external learning paths. The data does not say how these six domains compare in traffic or usefulness to readers, only their relative size in page count.
